title: When the Autopsy Falls
premise: Mara Vane, a retired detective turned failing bookshop owner, is paid a suspiciously large retainer by a nervous stranger named Elias Thorn to prove that his sister's death — scheduled, he insists, for the future — will be murder. When a woman matching his description turns up dead within days, Mara realizes Thorn was describing his own death and that her client may already be gone. Following a paper trail of forged autopsies tied to a contested inheritance, she hunts for Junie Calloway, a witness officially declared dead years ago whose testimony can void the statute. In the end, Mara finds Junie alive in hiding, exposes the coroner who falsified the reports, and must choose between protecting her found family at the bookshop and testifying to a truth that will burn her last bridges.
about_author: Noor Voss is a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where everyone claims to know everyone, which is exactly why she trusts no one.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A gaunt stranger named Elias Thorn walks into Vane & Daughters Books and pays three months' rent in cash to hire her — not to solve a murder, but to prevent one that hasn't happened yet. The beat: wary curiosity rekindling an instinct she thought retired.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Accidents
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with a flashback to the third 'accident' she quietly unraveled. She reviews her old case notes and finds a pattern: all three deaths involved the same probate attorney, Corliss Wren. Beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: A Client Who Won't Be Reached
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Thorn misses their first check-in; his hotel room is scrubbed and his sister denies having a brother. Beat: the cold realization that her client described his own death in past tense.

chapters.title: The Body That Wasn't His
chapters.summary: Detective Ivo Renk's POV. Renk, Mara's former protégé, catches a drowning case and recognizes Thorn's watch among the effects — but the dental records say otherwise. Beat: professional unease he can't file away.

chapters.title: Autopsy, Amended
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She pulls the autopsy report and finds a second version beneath the official one, signed by Dr. Pell Harrow, a coroner with a habit of closing files early. Beat: quiet fury at how neatly death has been paperwork.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Siege
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara and Tess (her shop assistant) POV. Someone ransacks the store overnight looking for something Thorn left behind; Tess, a runaway Mara took in, lies about what she saw. Beat: found family tested by secrets.

chapters.title: What Tess Kept
chapters.summary: Tess's POV. Confessing she hid a keycard Thorn slipped her, Tess and Mara decode it to a storage unit full of Wren's probate files. Beat: guilt transformed into alliance.

chapters.title: The Estate of Halcyon Marsh
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The files point to the Marsh inheritance: four heirs, three now dead by 'accident,' and one beneficiary — Wren himself, through a shell trust. Beat: the motive snaps into focus.

chapters.title: Renk Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Renk's POV. He confronts Mara about her fingerprints near the storage unit; old loyalty wars with new suspicion. Beat: the mentor-student bond cracking under procedure.

chapters.title: Junie Calloway, Deceased
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The estate's original witness, Junie Calloway, died seven years ago — or so says a death certificate signed by Harrow. But her signature on a recent postcard suggests otherwise. Beat: hope arriving disguised as an impossibility.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A lawyer friend explains the clock: Junie's sworn statement voids the trust only if filed within weeks. Beat: urgency reframing every choice as a countdown.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Niece
chapters.summary: Tess's POV. Following the postcard's postmark, Tess charms her way into a coastal village and hears of a woman who buys lamp oil but never shows her face. Beat: Tess stepping out of Mara's shadow.

chapters.title: Dead Woman Walking
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds Junie alive, living under a dead aunt's name, terrified because Harrow faked her death once and can make it real. Beat: fear met with stubborn compassion.

chapters.title: The Price of Testimony
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie recounts the night she saw Wren alter Halcyon Marsh's will, and why she let them bury her identity instead of her body. Beat: shame giving way to resolve.

chapters.title: An Accident, Scheduled
chapters.summary: Renk's POV. Renk discovers Harrow's amended autopsies match a pattern of insurance payouts routed through Wren's trust — and realizes Mara is next on the schedule. Beat: loyalty finally outweighing the rulebook.

chapters.title: Fire Sale
chapters.summary: Tess's POV. The bookshop is set ablaze as a warning; Mara and Tess salvage the case files from the smoke. Beat: loss crystallizing what they're fighting for.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Confession
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara corners Harrow with evidence of his forged certificates and offers him the one thing Wren never would: a way out. He gives her the trust's account numbers. Beat: a coward choosing, too late, to be brave.

chapters.title: Wren's Dinner Party
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wren invites Mara to a civilized negotiation — money for silence — and reveals he knows where Junie sleeps. Beat: velvet menace; the trap closing politely.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Buried
chapters.summary: Renk and Tess POV, alternating. While Wren dines with Mara, Renk moves Junie to safety through the storm, Tess running interference. Beat: the found family executing its first true plan together.

chapters.title: When the Autopsy Falls
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wren drops the civility; a struggle in his study ends with his own staged-accident machinery turned against him, recorded live by the pen camera Thorn left Mara. Beat: climax — truth delivered in the killer's own format.

chapters.title: Sworn
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie signs her statement before the statute expires; Harrow cooperates; Wren is charged across four counties. Beat: catharsis — the dead woman's name restored to the living.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue weeks later. The scorched bookshop reopens with a new shelf: case files bound like novels, Thorn's retainer framed unpaid. Renk brings coffee; Tess keeps the books; Junie visits under her real name. Beat: peace earned, doors open.
